newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE court to rule on Filipino death sentence appeal.
newsitem.headline: UAE court to rule on Filipino death sentence appeal.

text.p: A United Arab Emirates court will this month rule on an appeal by a Filipino sentenced to death for killing an Indian man, a defence lawyer said on Monday.
"The (Federal Supreme) court has reserved November 23 for judgment," said the lawyer who requested anonymity.
John Aquino was sentenced to death by a criminal court in the emirate of Ajman in 1989 for stabbing to death Harbajan Singh and the attempted murder of another Indian during an argument.
A higher court later upheld the death sentence.
The Philippines embassy has hired two lawyers for Aquino and has failed to persuade the victim's family to drop their demand for execution in return for so-called blood money, an embassy source said.
Embassy officials have also met senior UAE officials on Aquino's behalf and "exerted all efforts to protect his rights", another source said.
The Federal Supreme Court in Abu Dhabi makes the final ruling on death sentence cases, but any execution must be approved by UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan.

The UAE came under international criticism last year when a court sentenced Filipina maid Sarah Balabagan to death for stabbing her 70-year-old employer to death. She claimed he had tried to rape her.

Sheikh Zaid intervened and persuaded the victim's family to drop the death sentence in exchange for blood money. Balabagan returned to the Philippines in August after serving nine months of a one-year sentence.
